skill.name: knowledge-work-product-management
skill.description: Use when a product manager needs help writing feature specs, planning roadmaps, synthesizing user research, sending stakeholder updates, or analyzing the competitive landscape.
whenToUse: Writing a structured feature spec or PRD from a problem statement or feature idea
Creating, updating, or reprioritizing a roadmap in Now/Next/Later, quarterly, or OKR formats
Synthesizing interview notes, surveys, and tickets into themes, personas, and opportunity areas
Generating a stakeholder update or competitive brief tailored to a specific audience

keyConcepts.explanation: PRD structure, user stories, requirements categorization, and acceptance criteria to turn a problem statement into a full spec.
Prioritization frameworks like RICE and MoSCoW, multiple roadmap formats, and dependency mapping for roadmap management.
Thematic analysis, affinity mapping, persona development, and opportunity sizing to turn raw research into evidence-backed insights.
Update templates by audience (exec, engineering, customer), risk communication, and decision documentation, pulling context from connected tools.
competitive-brief builds feature comparison matrices, positioning, and win/loss analysis; metrics-review analyzes trends against targets with OKR-aligned tracking.
A sparring-partner mode using frameworks like How Might We, Jobs-to-be-Done, First Principles, and Opportunity Solution Trees to test assumptions and explore strategy.

gotchas: Stakeholder updates and metrics reviews are far richer when project trackers (Linear/Asana/Jira), analytics (Amplitude/Pendo), and Notion are connected via MCP
Without connected data sources you must provide roadmap, research, and metrics context manually
product-brainstorming intentionally pushes back and challenges assumptions rather than just generating ideas
The plugin is primarily designed for Cowork though it also runs in Claude Code
